questions.q: Define scalar multiplication of a matrix A = [aᵢⱼ] of order m × n by a scalar k. Write the resulting matrix's order and its (i, j)ᵗʰ element.
questions.a: Scalar multiplication kA produces a matrix of the same order m × n whose (i, j)ᵗʰ element is k·aᵢⱼ. A wrong answer (e.g., saying order changes to k×m × k×n, or element becomes aᵢⱼ + k) reveals confusion between scalar multiplication and matrix addition or matrix multiplication. Students often mistakenly think the scalar changes the matrix dimensions.

questions.q: Explain why k(A + B) = kA + kB holds for matrices A and B of the same order, but (k + l)A = kA + lA requires A to be a matrix and k, l to be scalars. What would go wrong if A and B had different orders in the first property?
questions.a: k(A + B) = kA + kB works because matrix addition is defined element-wise only for same-order matrices; if orders differ, A + B is undefined so the left side doesn't exist. (k + l)A = kA + lA uses scalar addition (k + l) which is always defined, then scalar multiplication. A wrong answer that ignores the same-order requirement for A + B shows the student doesn't grasp that matrix addition is a prerequisite for the distributive property to even be meaningful.

questions.q:
If A = 
⎡2  -1⎤
⎣3   4⎦
and B = 
⎡1   0⎤
⎣-2  5⎦
compute 3A - 2B. Show all steps.
questions.a:
Step 1: 3A = 3 × 
⎡2  -1⎤ = 
⎡6  -3⎤
⎣3   4⎦   ⎣9  12⎦

Step 2: 2B = 2 × 
⎡1   0⎤ = 
⎡2   0⎤
⎣-2  5⎦   ⎣-4  10⎦

Step 3: 3A - 2B = 
⎡6  -3⎤ - 
⎡2   0⎤ = 
⎡6-2  -3-0⎤ = 
⎡4  -3⎤
⎣9  12⎦   ⎣-4  10⎦   ⎣9-(-4)  12-10⎦   ⎣13  2⎦

A wrong answer like 
⎡4  -3⎤
⎣5   2⎦
(reveals subtracting 9 - 4 = 5 instead of 9 - (-4) = 13) shows sign error when subtracting negative elements — a very common mistake in board exams.

questions.q: Given matrices A (2×3) and B (2×3), and scalars k = 2, l = -3. Compare the results of (k + l)A and kA + lA. Then explain why the property (k + l)A = kA + lA would fail if we tried to apply it to (k + l)(A + B) without additional conditions.
questions.a: (k + l)A = (2 - 3)A = (-1)A = -A. kA + lA = 2A + (-3)A = 2A - 3A = -A. They are equal. For (k + l)(A + B), the left side is (k + l) times the matrix (A + B), which requires A + B to be defined (same order). The right side would be (k + l)A + (k + l)B by distributivity of scalar over matrix addition, which also requires A and B same order. The property doesn't "fail" — it's that (k + l)(A + B) = (k + l)A + (k + l)B is a different distributive law (scalar over matrix sum). A wrong answer confusing the two distributive laws reveals the student memorizes formulas without understanding the hierarchy: scalar addition → scalar multiplication → matrix addition.

questions.q:
A student solves for X in the equation 2X + 3A = 5B where 
A = 
⎡1  2⎤
⎣3  4⎦
, B = 
⎡2  0⎤
⎣1  3⎦
and writes:
2X = 5B - 3A
X = (5B - 3A)/2
Is this correct? If not, identify the error and give the correct steps.
questions.a:
The step X = (5B - 3A)/2 is notationally incorrect — matrix division is not defined. The correct step is X = ½(5B - 3A) or X = (1/2)(5B - 3A). The student treated scalar division like matrix division, which is a critical conceptual error. Correct steps:
5B = 
⎡10  0⎤
⎣5  15⎦
3A = 
⎡3  6⎤
⎣9  12⎦
5B - 3A = 
⎡7  -6⎤
⎣-4  3⎦
X = ½(5B - 3A) = 
⎡3.5  -3⎤
⎣-2   1.5⎦
Writing "/2" instead of "× ½" costs marks in board exams and shows misunderstanding of matrix algebra vs scalar algebra.

questions.q: Construct a real-world problem (Indian context: rupees, items, quantities) that requires scalar multiplication of a matrix and addition of two scaled matrices. Write the problem statement, set up the matrices, and show the computation.
questions.a:
Problem: A stationery shop sells notebooks (₹40), pens (₹10), and erasers (₹5). On Monday, they sold 20 notebooks, 50 pens, 30 erasers. On Tuesday, sales were 15 notebooks, 40 pens, 25 erasers. Represent Monday and Tuesday sales as column matrices M and T. If the shop owner wants to calculate total revenue for 3 Mondays and 2 Tuesdays combined, set up and solve.
M = 
⎡20⎤
⎢50⎥
⎣30⎦
, T = 
⎡15⎤
⎢40⎥
⎣25⎦
Price matrix P = [40  10  5] (row matrix).
Revenue for 3 Mondays = 3(P·M) = 3[40·20 + 10·50 + 5·30] = 3[800+500+150] = 3×1450 = ₹4350.
Revenue for 2 Tuesdays = 2(P·T) = 2[40·15 + 10·40 + 5·25] = 2[600+400+125] = 2×1125 = ₹2250.
Total = ₹6600.
Alternatively using matrix addition: 3M + 2T = 
⎡60⎤ + 
⎡30⎤ = 
⎡90⎤
⎢150⎥   ⎢80⎥   ⎢230⎥
⎣90⎦   ⎣50⎦   ⎣140⎦
Then P·(3M + 2T) = [40 10 5]·
⎡90⎤ = 40·90 + 10·230 + 5·140 = 3600+2300+700 = ₹6600.
⎢230⎥
⎣140⎦
A poor answer that only computes one day or forgets to multiply by the scalar shows inability to translate "3 Mondays" into 3M.

questions.q: Fill in the blank: Scalar ______ of a matrix is the operation of multiplying every element of an m × n matrix A = [aᵢⱼ] by a real number k (called a scalar), producing a new matrix kA = [k·aᵢⱼ] of the same order m × n.
Fill in the blank: Imagine a school canteen ______ tracking daily sales of three items — samosas, sandwiches, and juices — over a week using a 3 × 7 matrix where rows are items and columns are days.
What is Scalar multiplication of a matrix? State the definition given in this lesson.
questions.a: Scalar multiplication of a matrix is the operation of multiplying every element of an m × n matrix A = [aᵢⱼ] by a real number k (called a scalar), producing a new matrix kA = [k·aᵢⱼ] of the same order m × n.

questions.q: Fill in the blank: If the manager wants to project sales for a festival week where demand doubles, they simply multiply every entry by ______.
What common mix-up does this lesson flag about Scalar multiplication of a matrix?
questions.a: Students confuse scalar multiplication kA with matrix multiplication A × B.

questions.q: What must you be able to do to master this topic?
questions.a: The student must be able to: (1) compute scalar multiplication of matrices of any order correctly, showing element-wise multiplication; (2) apply the distributive properties k(A + B) = kA + kB and (k + l)A = kA + lA to simplify expressions; (3) compute expressions like 3A - 2B by first finding 3A and 2B separately then subtracting; (4).
